# Goals Model

The Goals Model says why: what the products must achieve, what stands in the way and what could help. Goals are rounded boxes, problems are hexagons, constraints are slanted boxes and opportunities are stadiums. An arrow `subgoal-of` points to the parent goal; dashed arrows show what hinders. Dashed grey boxes are elements of another scope.

Method: 4EM (Sandkuhl, Stirna, Persson and Wißotzki, *Enterprise Modeling: Tackling Business Challenges with the 4EM Method*, Springer 2014). Every element cites its source; `decided` means a source shows that the operator decided it.

Nothing is published, and the sources record no user count or request. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Choose a signal to read after publishing, such as downloads or issues, and write it down. | decided | hinders: [Publish the package for others to use](goals.md#goal-flow-publish) | [foldkit-flow:README.md:5][237], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/package.json:4][240], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="problem-flow-upstream-terms-open"></a><code>problem-flow-upstream-terms-open</code><br/>Problem | **Terms of the Foldkit offer remain to record.** The operator decided to offer the library as `@foldkit/flow` once its API settles. If Foldkit adopts it, the project publishes `@foldkit/flow` and deprecates `@tsukuri/flow`. What counts as settled, the date and the licence header are not yet recorded. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Record what counts as a settled API, the date and the licence header in a spec revision. | decided | hinders: [Offer the library to Foldkit](goals.md#goal-flow-upstream-offer) | [log L105][261], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:111][260], [foldkit-flow:STATE.md:13][259] |
| <a id="problem-flow-deferred-workflow-questions"></a><code>problem-flow-deferred-workflow-questions</code><br/>Problem | **Workflow hardening is deferred.** Vendoring Foldkit as a subtree, requiring human approval, signed commits and Renovate are all deferred. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Decide each item or record that it stays deferred. | decided | hinders: [Every change travels spec, code, PR](goals.md#goal-flow-lifecycle) | [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:112-113][279], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="problem-flow-lint-mocking-gap"></a><code>problem-flow-lint-mocking-gap</code><br/>Problem | **The module-mocking lint rule has a gap.** The lint rule that forbids module mocking matches only the `vitest` import source, so a mock imported from `vite-plus/test` passes. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Make the anti-slop module-mocking rule match the `vite-plus/test` source too. | decided | hinders: [Every change travels spec, code, PR](goals.md#goal-flow-lifecycle) | [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0001-first-felt-journey.md:142][280], [foldkit-flow:tools/oxlint/anti-slop/rules/no-module-mocking.ts:42-43][281], [issue foldkit-flow#5][282], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="problem-flow-community-files"></a><code>problem-flow-community-files</code><br/>Problem | **No security, conduct or contributing files.** The public repository has no SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. The README has a short contributing section. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Add the three files before the first publish. | decided | hinders: [Publish the package for others to use](goals.md#goal-flow-publish) | [absent foldkit-flow:SECURITY.md][268], [absent foldkit-flow:CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md][268], [absent foldkit-flow:CONTRIBUTING.md][268], [foldkit-flow:README.md:98-100][283], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-mit-licence"></a><code>constraint-flow-mit-licence</code><br/>Constraint | **The library is MIT licensed.** foldkit-flow is released under the MIT licence. Type: legal. | decided | constrains: [foldkit-flow](technical-components.md#comp-flow-product) | [log L48][17], [foldkit-flow:LICENSE:1-3][284], [foldkit-flow:README.md:96][285] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-public-repo"></a><code>constraint-flow-public-repo</code><br/>Constraint | **The repository is public and holds no secrets.** The repository is public. It never holds a secret or personal data. Type: organisational. | decided | constrains: [The project's own repository](actors-and-resources.md#resource-flow-repo) | [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:3][244], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:3][286], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-xyflow-notice"></a><code>constraint-flow-xyflow-notice</code><br/>Constraint | **Keep xyflow's licence notice and credit.** xyflow's code is MIT licensed. The project keeps its notice in NOTICE, credits it in the README and shows the credit link by default. An application may hide the link. Type: legal. | decided | constrains: [packages/flow (the library)](technical-components.md#comp-flow-library); hinders: [Publish the package for others to use](goals.md#goal-flow-publish) | [log L106][262], [foldkit-flow:NOTICE:4-17][263], [foldkit-flow:README.md:86][264], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:73][287] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-no-elk"></a><code>constraint-flow-no-elk</code><br/>Constraint | **ELK stays out of the library.** ELK.js is licensed EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0. It stays out of `packages/`, so the library does not depend on it. A private example may use it, and layout stays with the application. Type: legal. | decided | constrains: [packages/flow (the library)](technical-components.md#comp-flow-library) | [log L111][288], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:31][289], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:35][245], [foldkit-flow:README.md:7][246] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-effect-range"></a><code>constraint-flow-effect-range</code><br/>Constraint | **Cap the Effect range for unstable API use.** A package that uses an unstable or experimental Effect API accepts nothing above the next minor. Type: technical. | decided | constrains: [packages/flow (the library)](technical-components.md#comp-flow-library) | [log L55][19], [record foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:65][290], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/package.json:30-33][291] |
| <a id="constraint-flow-xyflow-pinned"></a><code>constraint-flow-xyflow-pinned</code><br/>Constraint | **Pin @xyflow/system exactly.** The library depends on `@xyflow/system` at the exact version 0.0.83, because a 0.0.x release may break. The project bumps the pin on purpose, and the journey gate decides each bump. Type: technical. | decided | constrains: [@xyflow/system](actors-and-resources.md#resource-flow-xyflow-system) | [log L107][292], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/package.json:18][293], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0001-first-felt-journey.md:42][294], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0001-first-felt-journey.md:111][295] |
| <a id="opportunity-flow-xyflow-core"></a><code>opportunity-flow-xyflow-core</code><br/>Opportunity | **Reuse xyflow's framework-free core.** React Flow and Svelte Flow share `@xyflow/system`, which holds pan and zoom, drag, handles, edge paths and the minimap. The Foldkit binding reuses it at an exact pin that the project bumps on purpose, instead of rewriting that interaction code. | decided | supports: [One felt journey works end to end](goals.md#goal-flow-first-journey) | [log L107][292], [foldkit-flow:README.md:86][264], [foldkit-flow:NOTICE:12-15][296] |
| <a id="opportunity-flow-other-foldkit-apps"></a><code>opportunity-flow-other-foldkit-apps</code><br/>Opportunity | **Other Foldkit apps can use it.** Foldkit app developers are the audience: a generic library with no product logic can serve any Foldkit application, and Foldkit itself may adopt it. The example app is the only consumer for now. | decided | supports: [Offer the library to Foldkit](goals.md#goal-flow-upstream-offer) | [log L48][17], [log L108][247], [foldkit-flow:STATE.md:13][259] |
| <a id="opportunity-flow-real-browser-defects"></a><code>opportunity-flow-real-browser-defects</code><br/>Opportunity | **A real browser finds defects unit tests miss.** Spec 0001 records that real Chromium runs found defects that unit tests missed: the connect gesture, the minimap, teardown, reconnect ends and the lazy cache. | decided | supports: [Prove interaction in a real browser](goals.md#goal-flow-browser-proof) | [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0001-first-felt-journey.md:130][256], [pr foldkit-flow#4][278], [log L118][22] |
| <a id="goal-flow-first-journey"></a><code>goal-flow-first-journey</code><br/>Goal | **One felt journey works end to end.** A person opens the example, sees a graph, pans and zooms, drags a node, connects two handles, reconnects an edge and selects by box. A keyboard-only person can select, move and delete nodes. Job: when I build a Foldkit application that shows a graph, I want a ready canvas with pan, zoom, drag, connect and selection, so that I do not write that interaction code myself. *Why proposed:* README line 5 says the first journey is built (spec 0001) and not published yet. Lines 20 and 66 list what it holds: pan and zoom, drag, connect and reconnect with validation, compound nodes, box select, minimap, zoom controls, fit view and node-level keyboard control. Keyboard connect is not built (line 78; see problem-flow-keyboard-connect-missing). The operator must accept this built journey as the first release scope, and confirm that the merged canvas is the intended first release. | proposed | subgoal-of: [A graph canvas for Foldkit applications](goals.md#goal-flow-vision) | [foldkit-flow:README.md:5][237], [foldkit-flow:README.md:20][238], [foldkit-flow:README.md:66][239], [foldkit-flow:README.md:78][273] |
| <a id="problem-flow-licence-scan-missing"></a><code>problem-flow-licence-scan-missing</code><br/>Problem | **No licence scan of published dependencies.** The operator decided to add a licence scan of the published dependencies, so that no copyleft licence reaches `packages/`. No gate runs it: the `ready` script lists no licence check. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Add a licence scan of the published dependencies to `ready` and CI, failing on an EPL or GPL licence. *Why open:* The operator decision (log line 111) adds the scan. The scripts in package.json line 13 show no licence gate at the pinned commit. | open | hinders: [MIT library, xyflow credited, no copyleft dependency](technical-components.md#req-flow-licence-hygiene) | [log L111][288], [foldkit-flow:package.json:13][297] |
| <a id="problem-flow-library-applies-deletion"></a><code>problem-flow-library-applies-deletion</code><br/>Problem | **The library applies a deletion itself.** The operator decided that the library reports outcomes and the app applies graph changes (log line 109). For a deletion, the Flow removes the deleted nodes and edges from its own Model and then reports them. **Gap in foldkit-flow.** Fix: Report a deletion as an outcome that the application applies, or record that the Flow's own Model is the application's. *Why open:* update.ts lines 289 to 343 remove the nodes and edges and report both sets. The log line does not say whether a deletion counts as a graph change that the app applies, or whether the Flow's own Model is the app's. The operator must say how "the app applies" reads for a deletion. | open | hinders: [Flow Submodel (Model, update, view)](technical-components.md#comp-flow-flow-submodel) | [log L109][298], [foldkit-flow:packages/flow/src/update.ts:289-343][299] |
